newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Alestra announces Oxxo, Bancomer alliance.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Alestra announces Oxxo, Bancomer alliance.

text.p: New Mexican telephone company Alestra said Tuesday that the bank branches of financial group Bancomer and convenience store Oxxo will receive ballots for users changing long-distance carriers from monopoly Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex).

In a statement, the joint venture between Mexican conglomerate Grupo Alfa, U.S. AT&T Corp and Mexico's Visa-Bancomer said: "Bancomer and Oxxo branches...have joined forces to collect preliminary long distance service registration tickets."
"With the program initiated by Bancomer and Oxxo, the public has the ease of being able to turn in the tickets at sites that they visit frequently," the statement said.
Oxxo is a subsidiary of Monterrey-based beverage company Femsa. Bancomer claims to have the largest number of bank branches in Mexico.
Mexico's local and long distance telephone service will open to competition in 1997, following years of monopoly service by Telmex.

Phone line owners are slated to receive tickets in their homes in the coming weeks that will allow them to pre-select a long distance carrier. They can also choose a carrier before each call by dialing a three-digit prefix.

Alestra spokeswoman Ana Maria Ruiz told Reuters that, in accordance to the government's schedule, the service will be offered initially only in the cities of Queretaro and Monterrey, and later throughout Mexico.
